title: Solutions and Concentration
seo_title: Chemistry 11: Solutions and Concentration Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Solution chemistry: solubility, dissociation of ionic compounds, molar concentration, dilution, precipitation reactions and net ionic equations, and acids, bases and titration. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Chemistry 11)
meta_desc: Free Chemistry 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): solutions, molarity, dilution and titration. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Molarity = moles of solute ÷ litres of solution.
body_html:
How to think about it

Ionic compounds dissociate into ions when they dissolve. Molar concentration C = n ÷ V (mol/L). When a solution is diluted, the moles of solute stay the same: C₁V₁ = C₂V₂. Solubility rules predict which ion pairs form a precipitate.

In a titration a solution of known concentration is added to a measured volume of an unknown until the end point; the volume used gives the unknown concentration through the mole ratio.

Example

0.50 mol of NaCl is dissolved to make 2.0 L. What is the concentration?

C = n ÷ V

Answer: 0.25 mol/L

Example

100 mL of 2.0 mol/L is diluted to 500 mL. New concentration?

C₂ = C₁V₁ ÷ V₂

Answer: 0.40 mol/L

Common mistakes

  • Using millilitres instead of litres in C = n ÷ V.
  • Thinking dilution changes the moles of solute.
  • Writing spectator ions in a net ionic equation.

items.q: 1.00 g of NaCl is dissolved in 250 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 58.5 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0.0171 ÷ 0.250 = 0.0684 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: 26 g of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is dissolved in 100 g of water. What is the mass percentage of the solute?
items.e: Mass % = mass of solute ÷ mass of solution × 100 = 26 ÷ 126 × 100 = 20.6%.

items.q: When salt dissolves in water to make salt solution, what is the solute?
